The *Kusalattika, Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 22.6) is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. As designated by its title, the text treats the analytical intersection of the triad of wholesome states (*kusalattika*) with the cluster of corruptions or taints (*āsavagocchaka*) within the conditional relations framework characteristic of the *Paṭṭhāna* [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan traditions are recorded for this section [DharmaNexus]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents extensive internal alignment within the Pali canonical Abhidhamma, registering 549 matches across 111 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial textual reuse occurs with other *Paṭṭhāna* chapters, including *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 16.25, with 45 shared passages), *Kusalattika, Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 22.5), *Kusalattika, Parittārammaṇattika* (Patthana 23.12), and *Kusalattika, Atītattikadvaya* (Patthana 23.17) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, substantial parallel phrasing is shared with other treatments of the taints cluster, such as *Hetuduka, Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 24.4 and 18.5) and *Sanidassanattika, Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 22.30) [DharmaNexus].
